newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Mobil Exploration and Production has begun the sale of the non-core assets it acquired through its A$1.8 billion takeover of Ampolex Ltd. The sell-off is expected to be very lucrative, with the Harriet and East Spar oil and gas fields on the North-West self alone expected to garner A$320 million for Mobil. Page 21.

Australia's biggest dairy co-operative, the Dairy Farmers Group, is considering being the first agricultural co-operative to list on the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX). Under new ASX regulations co-operatives would be able to capitalise their holdings without control being removed from members. Page 21.

The economic viability of BHP Steel's Project M, which utilises thin strip casing technology, is still uncertain. The process represents BHP's main opportunity to become a major steel maker in Asia as it has the potential to develop large market shares a demand increases in the region by making small capital outlay steel plants viable. Page 21.

Following the full deregulation of the telecommunications industry, Optus Communications has lost its monopoly on satellite services with the market now being open to international competitors. Optus will now have to compete with an aggressive regional space industry, with 22 Asia-Pacific satellites capable of beaming signals into Australia. Page 22.

Cigarette company Rothmans Holdings Ltd yesterday sparked a new price war with the launch of a new low-priced Holiday 20 brand. The move is expected to be matched by price discounts from main rivals Phillip Morris and WD & HO Wills Ltd. Page 23.

Boral Ltd announced yesterday it expects to reap an A$840 million profit from the sale of its gas distribution assets into the public float of its new subsidiary company, Envestra Ltd. In a statement Boral Ltd said arrangements had been finalised, and a prospectus for Envestra Ltd would be available in mid-July. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Insurance giant AMP has issued articles governing its demutualisation and future life as a listed company. These appear to give AMP directors unprecedented powers to restrict the activities of potentially hostile shareholders, to secure the positions of incumbent directors and managers, and to guard against takeover attempts. Page 23.

The New South Wales TAB yesterday recorded a small revenue growth for the 1996-97 financial year, achieving a net profit of A$118.5 million. The news bolsters the State Government's plans of selling the operation, from which it expects to raise up to A$15 billion. Page 25.

Macquarie Bank executive Simon Gautier Hannes is to face trial on separate charges relating to the 1996 takeover of TNT. St James Local Court magistrate Deborah Sweeney in the St James Local Court found that he had a case to answer on one insider trading charge which resulted in a A$2 million profit for Macquarie Corporate Finance. Page 23.

BHP may abandon its proposal for an offshore facility to process gas from the Undan-Bayu discovery, citing increased competition in the liquefied natural gas market in Australia. BHP has worked to secure the support of its major partner in the venture, US-based Phillips Petroleum, but the announcement in May that Shell and Woodside Petroleum were investigating similar projects has placed pressure on the proposal. Page 26.

The Federal Government is coming under increasing internal pressure to introduce the Collective Investments Bill which would increase protection for investors in unit trusts and other managed investment products. Chair of the Senate select committee on sperannuation Liberal Senator John Watson said last week that a new system for investor protection was required. Page 29.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The National Australia Bank is the likely winner of a bidding war for Advanta Corp, an American credit card company. Advanta has had an unsuccessful year, with bad debts hampering profits, but NAB believes its core skills and objectives are sound and the company will achieve good results from the move. Page 31.

Negotiations between Wesfarmers and ICI Australia's British-based parent, Imperial Chemical Industries plc, have broken down under threats of legal action by ICI Australia. Wesfarmers managing director Michael Chaney says the company will not make a furtHer bid. Page 31.

The Seven Network has acquired an additional A$135 million in MGM preferred stock, amid reports that MGM will advance a planned share offering from 1998 to later this year. The network is seeking a float from MGM's partner, Kirk Kerkorian, by the end of the year to benefit from a strong bull market. Page 31.

P&O chairman Lord Sterling claims Australian waterfront productivity has "slipped back quite heavily" after the Labor Government efficiency reforms of a few years ago. P&O is the owner of Conaust, a leading Australian stevedoring company, and Sterling beieves the balance of power on the waterfront should be in favour of management, not unions. Page 32.

Market analysts believe the Macquarie Bank's winning A$407.9 million bid for the Federal Government fleet management company DASfleet to be too high, with the value of the stock under question. Macquarie won the bid from the Commonwealth Bank and LeasePlan. Page 33.

Video group Network Entertainment says that despite a restructuring of operations, the company will make a loss for the 12 months to June, with shares in the company falling to 16 cents yesterday. The company says costs have fallen but this has not compensated for poor trading conditions. Page 35.
THE AGE

British telecommunications company Cable & Wireless has won board approval to gain control of Optus Communications by lifting its stake above 50 per cent. Cable & Wireless can only benefit from the deal if the float of Optus proceeds later this year, and if the move is approved by Treasurer Peter Costello and Communications Minister Richard Alston. Page B1.

Analysts believe the National Australia Bank is only a few weeks from finalising a deal to purchase American credit card company Advanta Corporation. If the acquisition proceeds, NAB's total assets will be raised to nearly A$210 billion, with the company likely to then make a major acquisition every few years. Page B1.

The May trade surplus of A$873 million was the highest ever, with the A$500 million sale of frigate Te Kaha to New Zealand being the major factor. Figures from the Bureau of Statistics show that seasonally adjusted exports rose by A$412 million in May toA$9.2 billion. Page B1.

Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer has supported claims by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade that tariff cuts are responsible for the quadrupling of manufactured exports since 1985. Farmers and wool growers have urged the Government to remove taiffs from the textile, clothing and footwear industry, and Fischer's comments are a positive move in that direction. Page B3.

Carlton & United Breweries has sold 10 million of its Crown casino shares at A$2.20 each, retaining 1.1 million shares, making a profit of A$22 million. Shares in Crown closed five cents higher at A$2.18 yesterday, with the first firm figures in the new venture expected in August. Page B3.

Macquarie Fleet leasing has won the race to buy the Federal Government's DASfleet at a cost of A$407.9 million. Macquarie will lease fleet vehicles back to the Government for five years, and will also be able to tender for non-government business. Page B4.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
